stem_text: A block of mass 5kg starting from rest is pulled up on a smooth inclined plane making an angle of 30^(∘) with horizontal with an effective acceleration of 1ms^(−2) . The power delivered by the pulling force at 𝑡=10s from the start is ___________ W. [use g=10ms^(−2) ] (calculate the nearest integer value)

candidate_solve.derivation: Incline angle 30 deg, acceleration a = 1 m/s^2. Equation of motion along incline: F_pull - m*g*sin(30) = m*a => F_pull = 5*10*0.5 + 5*1 = 25 + 5 = 30 N. At t = 10s: velocity v = a*t = 1 * 10 = 10 m/s. Instantaneous power P = F_pull * v = 30 * 10 = 300 W.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Newton's second law on incline to find pulling force, then instantaneous power P = F*v

representation_translation.evidence: Resolving gravity along 30 degree incline and kinematics v = a*t

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Find pulling force F = 30 N, speed at t=10s v = 10 m/s, evaluate power product

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Not confusing effective acceleration with pulling force alone

demand_proposal.rationale: Applying dynamics and kinematics to calculate instantaneous power delivery
